name: Acceleration and Sparse Structures
text:
# Acceleration and Sparse Structures


## Overview
[G] This family of methods accelerates [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) training and rendering by reducing the volume of space queried by the neural network, thereby lowering memory usage and computational cost. [G] It addresses the bottleneck where [standard NeRFs](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) sample uniformly across a large bounding box, evaluating the MLP in empty space or on transient objects. [G] It sets itself apart from [Training Ray Marching and Integration](2199-training-ray-marching-and-integration.md) by modifying *where* samples are taken (spatial constraints) rather than *how* they are integrated, and from [Adaptive Ray Sampling](8870-adaptive-ray-sampling.md) by using static or pre-computed geometric priors (hulls, blocks) rather than dynamic error metrics during training.

## Shared principles
[G] All methods in this family restrict the domain of the radiance field query. [G] Instead of evaluating the neural network $\mathcal{F}_\Theta$ at arbitrary points $\mathbf{x}$ within the scene bounding box $\mathcal{B}$, they define a subset $\mathcal{S} \subset \mathcal{B}$ such that $\mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{S}$ is required for evaluation. [G] This reduces the number of forward passes through the MLP. [G] The core mechanism is a culling step:
1. [G] Define a spatial constraint (e.g., visual hull, block grid, sparse cache).
2. [G] For each ray $\mathbf{r}(t) = \mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}$, compute the intersection of the ray with the constraint.
3. [G] Only evaluate $\mathcal{F}_\Theta(\mathbf{r}(t))$ for $t$ where $\mathbf{r}(t)$ lies within the constraint.

## Subtopics

### [Zip-NeRF Training Procedure](9538-zip-nerf-training-procedure.md)
A [two-stage inverse rendering optimization](#7387-two-stage-inverse-rendering-optimization.md) that uses a sparse Zip-NeRF radiance cache and a [fast cache](#9552-fast-cache-control-variate-radiance-cache.md) to decouple material/environment optimization from scene geometry. It sets itself apart by using a "gradient trick" to handle the non-analytic expected value of the radiance estimator, stabilizing the joint training of physically-based models. Choose this for high-fidelity inverse rendering where material and lighting parameters must be optimized alongside geometry.

### [VaxNeRF](11379-vaxnerf.md)
An [acceleration](#18-acceleration.md) strategy that restricts ray sampling to the **visual hull** $V$, the maximum volume compatible with object silhouettes from multi-view segmentation masks. It sets itself apart from [Zip-NeRF](9538-zip-nerf-training-procedure.md) by using a single MLP with uniform sampling inside $V$ rather than hierarchical caching. Choose this when coarse foreground-background segmentation masks are available and training speed is prioritized over handling complex transparency or transient objects.

### [Block-NeRF](13537-block-nerf.md)
Scales NeRFs to city-scale [scenes by partitioning](#8353-large-scene-reconstruction-via-chunking.md) the environment into overlapping spatial blocks, each trained with an independent NeRF model. It sets itself apart from [VaxNeRF](11379-vaxnerf.md) by using explicit spatial partitioning and multi-model composition rather than voxel-based culling. Choose this for large outdoor datasets where a single global NeRF is computationally infeasible and transient objects (pedestrians, cars) need to be masked out.

### Spatial Partitioning
A strategy to create tiles that ensures balanced workload (similar number of network evaluations/ray samples) across GPUs, avoiding suboptimal GPU utilization caused by uneven scene content distribution [S1]. If a sparse point cloud is available, recursively identify the plane where the Cumulative Distribution Function ([CDF](#19197-computational-deformation-field-cdf.md)) equals 0.5 for the 3D point distribution along each axis to partition space [S1]. If no sparse point cloud is available, discretize randomly sampled training rays into 3D samples to estimate scene content distribution, then partition similarly [S1]. Partitioning runs typically within seconds [S1].

## Background
[G] The concept of restricting NeRF queries to relevant volumes originated with early observations that uniform sampling wastes computation on empty space. [11379-vaxnerf.md] [VaxNeRF](#11379-vaxnerf.md) introduced the visual hull as a hard constraint. [13537-block-nerf.md] Block-NeRF addressed scalability by decomposing the scene. [9538-zip-nerf-training-procedure.md] Zip-NeRF introduced sparse caching for inverse rendering. [S1] Spatial partitioning for multi-GPU scaling was formalized in NeRF-XL.

## Sources
[S1] NeRF-XL: Scaling NeRFs with Multiple GPUs, https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-73195-2_6, fetched 2026-10-26
